notes: Shared by the Python pipeline and the browser demo. Patterns are case-insensitive and must stay compatible with both Python 're' and JavaScript RegExp (no lookbehind, no named groups). Placeholders {T}, {L}, {S} are expanded at load time. 'unless' suppresses a rule; 'value_min'/'value_max' compare capture group 1 (digits or number words).

rules.title: Decided at the landlord's sole discretion
rules.explanation: This clause lets one side decide on its own, with no objective standard and no way for you to challenge the decision.
rules.ask: Replace 'sole discretion' with an objective test (e.g. 'reasonable, documented costs') or require mutual agreement.

rules.title: You give up legal rights
rules.explanation: The clause asks you to waive rights or remedies you would otherwise have. Waivers like this are hard to undo once signed.
rules.ask: Strike the waiver, or limit it to a specific, named situation.

rules.title: Terms can be changed one-sidedly
rules.explanation: One party can change the agreement after you sign it, so the deal you agreed to may not be the deal you get.
rules.ask: Add: 'No change to this agreement is valid unless made in writing and signed by both parties.'

rules.title: Open-ended scope
rules.explanation: Words like 'whatsoever' or 'irrespective of the cause' make the obligation unlimited, including situations that are not your fault.
rules.ask: Limit the obligation to losses caused by your own negligence or breach.

rules.pattern: \b(?:shall not|cannot|will not|may not|agrees? not to|not to)\b{S}\b(?:approach|move|file|go to|initiate)\b{S}\b(?:court|tribunal|authority|legal proceedings?|rent controller)\b|\bwaives?\b{S}\bright to (?:approach|move|file)
rules.title: Blocks you from legal remedies
rules.explanation: The clause tries to stop you from going to a court or rent authority. You should never sign away access to dispute resolution.
rules.ask: Delete this clause; any dispute clause should apply equally to both parties.

rules.title: Non-refundable money
rules.explanation: Part of what you pay will not come back to you, even if you leave the property in perfect condition.
rules.ask: Ask for the full deposit to be refundable, minus documented damage beyond normal wear and tear.

rules.title: Deposit can be forfeited
rules.explanation: The landlord can keep the whole deposit as a penalty, not just the cost of actual damage or unpaid rent.
rules.ask: Limit deductions to unpaid rent and documented repair costs; remove forfeiture.

rules.title: Automatic deductions from deposit
rules.explanation: A fixed charge (often painting or cleaning) comes out of your deposit whatever condition you leave the home in. Repainting after normal use is usually ordinary wear and tear.
rules.ask: Make painting/cleaning deductions conditional on actual damage, with receipts.

rules.title: Clear refund deadline
rules.explanation: The deposit has a defined return deadline, which protects you from indefinite delays.

rules.title: Deductions must be justified
rules.explanation: Any deduction must be backed by an itemised statement or receipts, so you can check what you are charged for.

rules.title: Can be ended without reason or notice
rules.explanation: The tenancy can be ended at any time or without a reason, leaving you exposed to sudden loss of your home.
rules.ask: Require a written notice period (at least 1 month) and limit landlord termination to specific breaches.

rules.title: Lock-in period
rules.explanation: You cannot leave during the lock-in without a penalty. If your plans change (job, studies, family), you may still owe money.
rules.ask: Keep the lock-in short and make it apply to both sides equally.

rules.title: Pay rent for months you don't live there
rules.explanation: If you leave early you must pay rent for the rest of the term, which can be a large lump sum.
rules.ask: Cap early-exit cost at one month's rent, or allow you to leave once a replacement tenant is found.

rules.title: Only the landlord can end the agreement
rules.explanation: The right to terminate is one-sided. You are bound for the full term while the landlord is not.
rules.ask: Make termination rights and notice periods equal for both parties.

rules.title: Self-help eviction
rules.explanation: The landlord may cut utilities, change locks or remove your belongings. Evicting a tenant normally requires due legal process, not self-help.
rules.ask: Delete this clause entirely.

rules.pattern: \b(?:either party|both parties|either of the parties|either side)\b{S}\b(?:terminat|notice|vacat|end)|\b(?:terminat|notice)\w*{S}\b(?:by )?(?:either party|both parties)\b
rules.title: Mutual termination rights
rules.explanation: Both sides can end the agreement on the same terms, so neither party has an unfair advantage.

rules.title: Automatic renewal
rules.explanation: The agreement renews by itself unless someone gives notice in time. Miss the window and you can be bound for another term, often at a higher rent.
rules.ask: Put the notice deadline in your calendar, or ask for renewal only by mutual written agreement.

rules.title: Steep rent increase
rules.explanation: The rent rises by more than 10%, above the increases customary on renewal (often around 5-10%).
rules.ask: Negotiate a lower cap (e.g. 5%) or a fixed rent for the first renewal.

rules.pattern: \b(?:increase|enhance|escalat|hike|revis)\w*{S}\b(?:as (?:decided|determined|fixed) by|at the (?:sole )?discretion|prevailing market|market rate|as (?:he|she|they|the {L}) (?:may )?(?:deems?|thinks?|considers?) fit|from time to time|whenever)\b|\b{L}\s+(?:may|can|shall be entitled to)\s+(?:at any (?:time|point) )?(?:increase|revise|enhance|demand an increased)\b(?![^.]*(?:%|percent|per cent))|\b(?:fix|decide|determine)\w* any rent\b|\brent\b{S}\bdecided by the {L}
rules.title: Rent increase with no cap
rules.explanation: The rent can be raised without a fixed limit, so you cannot predict what renewal will cost.
rules.ask: Ask for a fixed percentage cap written into the agreement.

rules.title: Renewal at your option
rules.explanation: You decide whether to renew, which gives you security of tenure.

rules.pattern: \b(?:not (?:exceed|be more than|more than)|maximum of|capped at|at most)\s*(?:\w+\s*)?(?:\(\d+\)\s*)?\d*\s*(?:%|percent|per cent)
rules.title: Rent increase is capped
rules.explanation: Any increase is limited to a stated maximum, so future rent is predictable.

rules.title: You pay for all repairs
rules.explanation: Making you responsible for every repair includes major and structural problems that are normally the landlord's job.
rules.ask: Split responsibilities: minor day-to-day repairs for you, major/structural repairs for the landlord.

rules.pattern: \b{T}\b{S}\b(?:repair|replace|bear|pay)\w*{S}\b(?:structural|roof|foundation|walls?|pipelines?|wiring)\b|\b(?:structural|major)\b{S}\b(?:borne|paid) by (?:the )?{T}\b|\b(?:roof|structural|foundation|overhead (?:water )?tank|drainage|main (?:water|drainage|sewer)\w*)\b{S}\b(?:responsibility of|borne by|paid by|done by|carried out by) (?:the )?{T}\b
rules.title: Structural repairs on you
rules.explanation: Structural repairs (roof, walls, main plumbing or wiring) are expensive and are normally the owner's responsibility.
rules.ask: Make structural and major repairs the landlord's responsibility.

rules.pattern: \b(?:including|irrespective of|regardless of|even if due to)\b{S}\b(?:(?:normal|reasonable|fair|ordinary) (?:wear and tear|use)|ageing|aging|natural deterioration)\b
rules.title: Charged for normal wear and tear
rules.explanation: You can be charged for the natural ageing of the home from ordinary use, which tenants usually aren't liable for.
rules.ask: Add 'normal wear and tear excepted'.

rules.pattern: \b(?:except|excepting|excluding|other than|save for|barring|subject to)\b{S}\b(?:normal|reasonable|fair|ordinary) wear and tear\b|\b(?:normal|reasonable|fair|ordinary) wear and tear (?:excepted|exempted|being excepted)\b
rules.title: Normal wear and tear excluded
rules.explanation: You aren't charged for ordinary ageing of the property.

rules.title: Landlord handles major repairs
rules.explanation: The landlord is responsible for major or structural repairs, as is standard.

rules.title: High monthly interest on late payment
rules.explanation: Interest of 2% or more per month is 24%+ per year, far above normal lending rates.
rules.ask: Ask for a modest flat late fee or a low annual interest rate.

rules.title: Daily penalty
rules.explanation: Charges that accrue every day add up quickly, especially if a payment is delayed by a bank holiday or an emergency.
rules.ask: Ask for a grace period and a capped one-time late fee.

rules.title: Penalty of multiple times the rent
rules.explanation: Overstaying or a breach costs double (or more) the rent, a penalty far larger than the landlord's actual loss.
rules.ask: Replace with ordinary per-day rent for any overstay agreed in writing.

rules.title: Grace period for payment
rules.explanation: You get extra days to pay before any penalty applies.

rules.pattern: \b(?:enter|entry|access|inspect\w*|visit|show)\b{S}(?:\bat any (?:time|hour)\b|\bany time\b|\bwithout (?:any )?(?:prior )?(?:notice|intimation|informing)\b|\bwith or without (?:prior )?notice\b|\bat all times\b|\bwhenever (?:he|she|they|it)? ?(?:wish|like|want|choose)e?s?\b)|\bsurprise (?:inspections?|visits?)\b|\bunrestricted access\b|\bfree access\b
rules.title: Landlord can enter without notice
rules.explanation: The landlord can come into your home whenever they like, which affects your privacy and security.
rules.ask: Require at least 24 hours' written notice except in a genuine emergency.

rules.title: Landlord keeps a key
rules.explanation: The landlord keeps a key to your home, so entry is possible without you knowing.
rules.ask: Ask that keys be used only in emergencies or with your consent.

rules.pattern: \b(?:\d+|one|two|twenty[- ]four|forty[- ]eight|seventy[- ]two)\s*(?:\(\d+\)\s*)?(?:hours?|days?)'?s?\s*(?:prior |advance )?(?:written )?notice\b|\breasonable (?:prior |advance )?(?:written )?notice\b|\bprior (?:written )?(?:notice|appointment|intimation)\b|\bwith the (?:prior )?(?:consent|permission) of the {T}\b|\bnot enter\b{S}\bwithout\b{S}\b(?:consent|permission|notice)\b|\bin the presence of the {T}
rules.title: Entry only with notice
rules.explanation: The landlord must give advance notice before entering, protecting your privacy.

rules.title: Broad indemnity
rules.explanation: You agree to cover the landlord's losses or claims broadly, possibly including ones you did not cause.
rules.ask: Limit the indemnity to losses caused by your negligence or breach of the agreement.

rules.title: Landlord excluded from all liability
rules.explanation: The landlord is not responsible for losses or injuries, even ones caused by poor upkeep of the building.
rules.ask: Add an exception for loss caused by the landlord's negligence or failure to repair.

rules.title: Liability limited to fault
rules.explanation: Responsibility depends on who was actually at fault, which is fair to both sides.

rules.title: Restrictions on guests
rules.explanation: You need permission to have guests, which reaches into your private life in your own home.
rules.ask: Limit restrictions to long-term additional occupants, not ordinary visitors.

rules.title: Consent can't be unreasonably refused
rules.explanation: The landlord must have a good reason to say no, which keeps the permission process fair.

rules.title: No proof of payment
rules.explanation: Paying without receipts leaves you with no proof that rent was paid if a dispute arises.
rules.ask: Pay by bank transfer/UPI or insist on signed receipts.

rules.title: Rent receipts provided
rules.explanation: You get written proof of each payment.

rules.pattern: \b{T}\b{S}\b(?:property tax|house tax|municipal tax(?:es)?)\b|\b(?:property tax|house tax|municipal tax(?:es)?)\b{S}\b(?:borne|paid) by (?:the )?{T}\b
rules.title: Owner's taxes passed to you
rules.explanation: Property/municipal tax is normally the owner's liability; this clause shifts it to you.
rules.ask: Ask that property and municipal taxes stay with the owner.

rules.title: No upper limit
rules.explanation: The amount you can be asked to pay has no ceiling.
rules.ask: Ask for a fixed cap on the amount.

rules.title: You pay the landlord's legal costs
rules.explanation: You cover the landlord's lawyer fees, even when the landlord is in the wrong or the paperwork benefits them.
rules.ask: Each party should bear its own legal costs, or costs should follow the outcome of a dispute.

rules.title: Landlord picks the arbitrator
rules.explanation: Disputes go to an arbitrator chosen by the landlord alone, which is not a neutral forum.
rules.ask: Ask for an arbitrator appointed jointly, or keep access to the Rent Authority/courts.

rules.title: Changes need both signatures
rules.explanation: The agreement can only be changed with both parties' written signatures, so nothing changes behind your back.

rules.title: Landlord confirms ownership
rules.explanation: The landlord confirms they own the property and can rent it out, which protects you from a disputed tenancy.

rules.title: Large advance rent
rules.explanation: Several months of rent are paid up front, so a lot of your money is locked in before you even move in.
rules.ask: Limit advance rent to one month.

rules.title: Rent fixed for the term
rules.explanation: Your rent cannot go up during the agreement.

rules.title: Deposit of several months' rent
rules.explanation: The deposit equals several months of rent, which is a lot of your money held by the landlord. India's Model Tenancy Act, 2021 suggests a cap of two months' rent for homes (only in states that have adopted it).
rules.ask: Negotiate the deposit down to 2-3 months' rent.

rules.pattern: \bdeposit\b{S}\b(?:not exceed|maximum of|capped at|limited to|no more than)\b
rules.title: Deposit is capped
rules.explanation: The deposit amount is limited, keeping more of your money with you.

rules.title: Interest if the deposit is late
rules.explanation: The landlord pays you interest if the deposit is returned late, which encourages on-time refunds.

rules.pattern: \bjoint(?:ly)? inspect|\bjoint inspection\b|\binspect\w*{S}\bin the presence of both\b
rules.title: Joint inspection before deductions
rules.explanation: Damage is assessed together with you, so you can dispute claims on the spot.

rules.title: Very short notice to vacate
rules.explanation: The landlord can end the tenancy with under a month's notice, which is very little time to find a new home.
rules.ask: Ask for at least one month's written notice.

rules.title: Must leave immediately
rules.explanation: You may have to leave within hours or immediately, with no time to find another home.
rules.ask: Require at least 30 days' written notice and a chance to fix any breach.

rules.title: Landlord can end it only for a reason
rules.explanation: The landlord can only end the tenancy for a real breach, and you get a chance to fix it first.

rules.title: Early exit without penalty
rules.explanation: You can leave early in the stated situations without paying a penalty.

rules.title: Repainting regardless of condition
rules.explanation: You must pay for repainting whatever state the home is in. Repainting after normal use is usually the owner's cost.
rules.ask: Make repainting conditional on damage beyond normal wear and tear.

rules.title: Replace items with new ones
rules.explanation: If something the landlord supplied breaks, even from age, you must buy a new one.
rules.ask: Limit this to damage you caused; normal breakdowns should be the owner's cost.

rules.title: Liable for damage you didn't cause
rules.explanation: You pay for damage from events outside your control, such as natural disasters or leaks from neighbours.
rules.ask: Limit your liability to damage caused by you, your family or guests.

rules.pattern: \b{L}\b{S}\brepair\w*{S}\bwithin\b|\bfailing which,? the {T} may\b|\bdeduct the cost from the rent\b
rules.title: Repairs within a deadline
rules.explanation: The landlord must fix problems within a set time, and you have a remedy if they don't.

rules.title: Landlord accepts liability
rules.explanation: The landlord takes responsibility for losses caused by the building's condition.

rules.title: Pay dues from before you moved in
rules.explanation: You may be charged for unpaid bills or society dues that belong to an earlier period.
rules.ask: Make dues before your move-in date the owner's responsibility.

rules.title: Restrictions on your personal life
rules.explanation: The clause controls private choices (food, who visits, when you come home) that have nothing to do with protecting the property.
rules.ask: Ask to remove lifestyle restrictions not tied to damage or nuisance.

rules.title: Explicit freedom of use
rules.explanation: The agreement confirms things you are allowed to do, avoiding later disputes.

rules.pattern: \b(?:fail\w*|default\w*|breach\w*|violat\w*|non-?compliance|contravene\w*)\b{S}\b(?:automatic(?:ally)? terminat\w*|stand terminated|immediate(?:ly)? terminat\w*|terminat\w* (?:immediately|forthwith|automatically)|(?:cause|grounds?) for (?:immediate )?termination|self[- ]?evict\w*|vacate (?:immediately|forthwith))|\b(?:automatic(?:ally)? terminat\w*|stand terminated|cause for (?:immediate )?termination|grounds? for termination)\b{S}\b(?:fail\w*|default\w*|breach\w*|violat\w*|non-?compliance)\b
rules.title: Ended for any breach
rules.explanation: The agreement can end automatically or immediately for any failure to comply, however small, with no notice or chance to fix it.
rules.ask: Limit termination to serious breaches, after written notice and at least 15-30 days to remedy.

rules.title: You repair or replace items
rules.explanation: You must pay to repair or replace fixtures and appliances, which may include breakdowns from age or normal use.
rules.ask: Limit this to damage caused by you or your guests; normal breakdowns should be the owner's cost.

rules.title: You pay legal or collection costs
rules.explanation: You must pay the landlord's lawyer or collection costs, which can add up quickly in any dispute.
rules.ask: Each party should bear its own legal costs, or costs should follow the outcome.
